transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-11
- Time: 09:32 PST
- Duration: ~56 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Head of Search, Peregrine), Ravi Singh (ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Platform)

Optional summary: (auto) Quick discovery on Peregrine's plan to add embeddings+rerank into their search flow, evaluation of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, vector DB integration questions, throughput/latency targets, and next steps to run a short POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro: I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Jordan our SE will do the deep dive on embeddings/rerank. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Liam: good, thanks Maya. we've been talking to a couple providers, want to see how Redwood fits for embeddings + a rerank step in our pipeline.
[00:12] Jordan (Redwood SE): awesome. to kick off, can you give us the context — current stack, qps, latency targets, and what you mean by rerank?
[00:22] Liam: sure. currently we run OpenSearch for our main search; classic BM25 for recall then a small ML model to rerank top 50. we're thinking of moving to embedding-based candidate retrieval, then a cross-encoder rerank for better relevance. target tail latency for rerank step is ~100-200ms for most queries, and throughput around 200 qps peak.
[00:42] Ravi: our embeddings are 1536-d (we use a public model). storage is in S3, index in Pinecone today for a subset. but Pinecone's cost is creeping up as we scale and cold start latencies are a bit variable.
[00:55] Jordan: ok, good. a few high-level axes: index/store (vector DB), embeddings model and dimensionality, retrieval strategy (ANN/IVF/HNSW), and rerank model (cross-encoder on GPU). do you plan hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings) or pure vector first?
[01:10] Liam: hybrid ideally for shopping queries; BM25 + embedding similarity then rerank. need to keep recall on tail queries.
[01:17] Maya: do you have any constraints around PII/data residency or SSO?
[01:22] Sofia: yes — SOC 2 required, we need audit logs and SAML SSO. also would prefer VPC/private deployment for some regulated customers, but we could pilot on hosted.
[01:31] Jordan: makes sense. Redwood Hosted supports SOC2 and audit logs; for VPC and stricter network controls we recommend Dedicated or Private depending on your needs. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; Private gives customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:45] Ravi: can you clarify latency differences between Hosted and Dedicated?
[01:49] Jordan: Hosted is multi-tenant and optimized for quick time-to-value; typical median token latencies are low but tail can vary depending on load. Dedicated puts you on reserved pods — consistent throughput and more predictable tail latency since you're not sharing. For a cross-encoder rerank at 200 qps, Dedicated sizing will depend on model size and sequence length.
[02:08] Liam: model size — we're thinking a 1.3B cross-encoder for rerank. embeddings are served from a 1536-d transformer. how many GPUs do we need?
[02:18] Jordan: rough rule: for 1.3B cross-encoder with batch optimizations, you can get ~50-100 qps per GPU depending on sequence length and kernel optimizations. for 200 qps you may want 2-4 GPUs with concurrency and batching tuned. Jordan: also our runtime supports quantized execution paths and attention optimizations to push throughput.
[02:35] Ravi: what's the workflow for storing embeddings? do we have to use Pinecone or can we integrate our existing OpenSearch or Milvus?
[02:42] Jordan: Redwood does not force a specific vector DB. Many customers keep embeddings in their vector DB — Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, or even an ANN layer sitting on top of OpenSearch — and call Redwood for embedding generation and the rerank model. We also offer managed indexes for hosted cases, but for Dedicated/Private we commonly see customers run their vector index in their environment and call Redwood for model inference.
[03:02] Sofia: network wise, if we run Dedicated, does traffic to the vector DB cross the internet? we want minimum egress.
[03:09] Jordan: for Dedicated in a cloud region we can arrange peering or VPC egress controls; for Private you run the whole inference inside your VPC so there's no public egress. we'll loop in Solutions Arch for a topology diagram.
[03:22] Liam: on dimensionality — do you recommend 1536 vs 768 vs larger? cost tradeoffs?
[03:27] Jordan: higher dims give better representational power but higher storage and compute for ANN searches. many customers find 1536 a good balance; 768 works if you have strict cost limits. also Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and hybrid rerank configs: use lower-dim approximate retrieval then full-dim rerank on top-k to save cost.
[03:45] Maya: curious about hybrid search patterns — what's typical at scale?
[03:48] Jordan: common pattern: BM25 or lexical-first to narrow candidate set, then ANN on embeddings to get top 200, then cross-encoder rerank top 30. This keeps end-to-end latency bounded. Also prefix/KV cache for frequent queries reduces cost.
[04:05] Ravi: what's the integration surface? We have search infra in k8s; how does Redwood client call fit in?
[04:11] Jordan: you call Redwood's REST/SDK to generate embeddings (or host embeddings on Redwood), and call cross-encoder endpoints for rerank. For Dedicated you can have private endpoints in your VPC. Typical flow: index build job writes embeddings to vector DB, query flow reads candidates from vector DB, then sends batched rerank requests to Redwood endpoint.
[04:28] Liam: what about batching? our query mix is spiky at noon; we care about tail.
[04:33] Jordan: Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and smart batching policies. For low-latency rerank we tune max latency budget so batches form but don't exceed SLO. Also there's automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
[04:44] Sofia: security: KMS integration for keys? audit logs?
[04:48] Jordan: yes KMS for Private/Dedicated, HSM options for enterprise, audit logs and token-level tracing in the Console. We have SOC 2 docs and SAML SSO support. I'll share the security pack.
[04:58] Liam: you'd mentioned quantization — does that impact quality for rerank?
[05:02] Jordan: quantization mainly helps throughput for autoregressive generators; for cross-encoder rerank we recommend mixed precision or int8 on GPU — quality impact is small if you calibrate. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles by workload.
[05:14] Ravi: for the ANN side — do you have recommended index parameters for 1536 dims at our scale (millions of vectors)?
[05:20] Jordan: typical is HNSW with M tuned to balance recall, efConstruction and efSearch tuned for your recall/latency tradeoff. For millions, you can expect sub-20ms search times for ANN on optimized hardware, but that depends on the vector DB — Redwood will run benchmarks during the POC to calibrate.
[05:35] Liam: any customers you can point to with a similar stack?
[05:38] Maya: yes, we recently worked with Aurora (retail) on embeddings+ranks — they kept OpenSearch for lexical and used Redwood for cross-encoder rerank; saw a recall improvement of ~12% while maintaining a 120ms rerank tail. I can share the case study.
[05:51] Ravi: cost question — Hosted vs Dedicated pricing math for heavy rerank: what's the unit economics?
[05:57] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based (per-inference tokens/units) which is great for POCs and variable traffic. Dedicated has a reserved capacity model with monthly commits — more predictable and lower per-unit cost once utilization is high. We can run a cost model in the sizing doc I'll send.
[06:13] Liam: we'd like a POC: run our 1k queries, measure recall lift and end-to-end latency with Redwood rerank. timeline?
[06:19] Maya: sounds good. proposed plan: 1) quick smoke on Hosted to validate quality 2) 1-week Dedicated POC in a sandbox or Private if you prefer VPC 3) sizing & contract. does that map?
[06:31] Sofia: pilot on Hosted first, but we need SOC2 docs before any data sharing. if Hosted is ok for smoke we'll start there; but ideally Dedicated for the 1-week heavy benchmark.
[06:40] Maya: noted. we'll send SOC2 and security pack, and Jordan will share the benchmark harness.
[06:46] Ravi: small nit — our ML team also wants to try 768-d embeddings as a lower-cost baseline. can we run both dims in the POC?
[06:52] Jordan: yes, we'll instrument both and run A/B to measure quality vs cost.
[06:56] Liam: any gotchas with cold-start/kv caching and rerank?
[06:59] Jordan: KV cache helps generative workloads; for rerank cross-encoder it's less applicable, but we do caching for repeated queries and prefix caching for embeddings. Also model warm pools on Dedicated reduce cold-starts.
[07:11] Maya: ok let's capture next steps and action items.
[07:14] Maya (brief recap): 1) We (Redwood) send security pack + SOC2 + VPC docs. 2) Maya send Dedicated sizing & pricing. 3) Jordan share rerank harness and scripts. 4) Peregrine to send sample queries and infra diagram. 5) Schedule POC kickoff.
[07:30] Liam: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:33] Sofia: thanks, bye.

End transcript.
